"""Exact finite telemetry rule compiler (NetNomos protocol v2.1).

Every object in this model is finite: windows range over the declared
Cartesian product of the field domains, clauses are disjunctions of the
input predicates and theories are conjunctions of clauses.  The compiler
therefore answers discovery, certification and decoding questions with
exact integer bitset arithmetic instead of sampling or heuristics:

* discovery enumerates the inclusion-minimal disjunctions satisfied by all
  training windows (conditions 1 and 2) and keeps those falsified somewhere
  in the declared universe (condition 3);
* certificates are the smallest training index at which a literal is the
  only true literal of its clause, plus the smallest universe index that
  falsifies the whole clause;
* decoding counts and extends completions of the operator-approved theory
  under fixed bindings and a target prefix.
"""

        """All eligible inclusion-minimal disjunctions with certificates.

        A clause qualifies when it holds on every training window, loses that
        property when any literal is dropped, and is falsified by at least one
        window of the declared universe.  Clauses with the first property are
        exactly the minimal members of the family whose literal-wise
        falsification sets have an empty intersection, so a depth-first
        enumeration of that family is exhaustive.
        """
        if not self._prepared:
            self._predicate_masks()
        width = self.width
        # falsified-set bitsets over the training rows and over the universe
        train_false = [self.train_full & ~mask for mask in self._train_true]
        universe_false = [self.universe_full & ~mask for mask in self._universe_true]
        # A literal that is true on no training window can never be the only
        # true literal of its clause, and a literal that is true throughout the
        # declared universe blocks condition 3; neither can occur in a rule, so
        # the enumeration may skip such literals outright.
        eligible = [train_true != 0 and universe_false[literal] != 0
                    for literal, train_true in enumerate(self._train_true)]
        count = self.predicate_count
        found: list[tuple[tuple[int, ...], list[int], int]] = []
        full = self.train_full

        def emit(clause, prefixes, counter_mask):
            size = len(clause)
            suffixes = [full] * (size + 1)
            for position in range(size - 1, -1, -1):
                suffixes[position] = suffixes[position + 1] & train_false[clause[position]]
            witnesses = []
            for position in range(size):
                # rows where every other literal is false; clause validity
                # then forces this literal to be the only true one
                others = prefixes[position] & suffixes[position + 1]
                if others == 0:
                    return
                witnesses.append(lowest_bit(others))
            if counter_mask == 0:
                return  # no window of the declared universe falsifies it
            found.append((clause, witnesses, lowest_bit(counter_mask)))

        def walk(chosen, prefixes, and_value, universe_value):
            start = chosen[-1] + 1 if chosen else 0
            depth = len(chosen)
            for literal in range(start, count):
                if not eligible[literal]:
                    continue
                value = and_value & train_false[literal]
                clause = chosen + (literal,)
                counter = universe_value & universe_false[literal]
                if value == 0:
                    # every training window satisfies the clause
                    emit(clause, prefixes, counter)
                    # any strict superset keeps that property, so dropping the
                    # added literal can never be witnessed: do not extend
                    continue
                if depth + 1 < width:
                    walk(clause, prefixes + [value], value, counter)

        walk((), [full], full, self.universe_full)
        found.sort(key=lambda item: (len(item[0]), item[0]))
        return [
            {'clause': list(clause), 'witnesses': witnesses, 'counterexample': counter}
